Definition: properly, to intertwine or contract, i.e. (by implication) to shrivel (as with heat); figuratively, to be deeply affected with passion (love or pity)
BiblicalUsage: Kamar is the inward burning — bowels yearning, a heart turned within, skin blackened like an oven. Joseph's bowels yearned upon his brother; the true mother's bowels yearned upon her son; God says His heart is turned within Him toward Ephraim; and Jerusalem says her skin was black like an oven because of famine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word shows that God's compassion is not cool and distant. His bowels yearn, His heart turns within Him — the same inward fire that marks a mother's love marks His, and that is why I trust Him with my own yearnings.
